questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a thermal decomposition reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 3**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thermal decomposition reaction** is a type of chemical reaction where a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances when heated.
 
• In the given options, **ZnCO3 → ZnO + CO2** (option 3) is an example of a thermal decomposition reaction.
 
• When zinc carbonate (ZnCO3) is heated, it decomposes into zinc oxide (ZnO) and carbon dioxide (CO2).
 
• Other options like the decomposition of water (H2O) and sodium chloride (NaCl) involve different types of reactions such as electrolysis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thermal decomposition** reactions require energy in the form of heat to break chemical bonds in the compound undergoing decomposition.
 
• Common examples of thermal decomposition reactions include the breakdown of calcium carbonate (CaCO3) into calcium oxide (CaO) and carbon dioxide (CO2), and the decomposition of potassium chlorate (KClO3) into potassium chloride (KCl) and oxygen (O2).
 
• These reactions are important in various industrial processes, such as the production of lime from limestone and the preparation of oxygen in laboratories.

questions.question: What is the name of the Medium Altitude Long Endurance (MALE) drone discussed at the Drone Industry Conclave 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**TAPAS**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **TAPAS** is a Medium Altitude Long Endurance (MALE) unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) in India.
 
• The UAV is designed for **surveillance, reconnaissance, and intelligence gathering** over extended periods.
 
• TAPAS was showcased at the Drone Industry Conclave 2025 as a significant step towards **India's self-reliance in drone technology**.
 
• It can operate at altitudes of up to 30,000 feet and has an endurance of over 24 hours, making it suitable for both military and civilian applications.
 
• The drone integrates advanced systems such as **electro-optical payloads, synthetic aperture radar, and satellite communication capabilities**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Medium Altitude Long Endurance (MALE) UAVs**

 
 
• MALE UAVs are designed to operate at altitudes ranging from 10,000 to 30,000 feet.
 
• These drones are capable of long-duration flights, often exceeding 24 hours, making them ideal for extended missions.
 
• They are widely used for surveillance, reconnaissance, and intelligence gathering, particularly in defense and border monitoring.
 
 
 
• **DRDO's Role in UAV Development**
 
 
• The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) is India's premier research agency focused on defense technology.
 
• It has developed several UAVs, including TAPAS, RUSTOM, and NETRA, to strengthen India's indigenous drone capabilities.
 
• DRDO collaborates with other agencies and private industries to integrate cutting-edge technologies into its UAV projects.
 
 
 
• **Applications of TAPAS**
 
 
• Military: Border surveillance, anti-terror operations, and intelligence gathering.
 
• Civilian: Disaster management, agriculture monitoring, and search-and-rescue operations.
 
• Scientific: Environmental data collection and weather monitoring.
 
 
 
• **Other UAVs Developed by DRDO**
 
 
• **RUSTOM:** Another MALE UAV designed for tactical missions and surveillance.
 
• **NETRA:** A small quadcopter UAV used for surveillance in urban areas.
 
• **AURA:** An autonomous stealth UAV under development for advanced military applications.

questions.question: For which discovery was the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics awarded?

options.text: Observation of quantum tunneling in superconducting circuits and HVAC systems
Experimental verification of quantum coherence in large-scale systems
Demonstration of quantum state transitions in Josephson junction arrays
Discovery of macroscopic quantum mechanical tunneling and energy quantization in electric circuits

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Discovery of macroscopic quantum mechanical tunneling and energy quantization in electric circuits.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

 
• **The 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to John Clarke, Michel H. Devoret, and John M. Martinis for their discovery of macroscopic quantum mechanical tunneling and energy quantization in electric circuits.**
 
• The laureates proved that quantum phenomena could exist at a macroscopic scale using superconducting circuits with Josephson junctions.
 
• Their experiments showed that these circuits absorb and emit energy in discrete amounts, validating the principle of energy quantization.
 
• The discovery established that large-scale electrical systems can behave as unified quantum objects.
 
• This foundational work became a cornerstone for modern quantum technologies such as quantum computers, quantum cryptography, and quantum sensors.

questions.question: Which article of the Constitution of India guarantees equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment and appointment to any office under the state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 16.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 16**

 
 
• **Article 16 of the Constitution of India** guarantees equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment and appointment to any office under the state.
 
• All citizens shall have an equal opportunity to apply for jobs or be **appointed to positions within the state.**
 
• **No citizen **will be excluded from or subject to discrimination in connection with any employment or office under the State solely on the basis of **religion, race, caste, sex, or descent.**
 
• Nothing in this article shall prevent **Parliament** from passing a law specifying a requirement for residence within a **State or Union territory** prior to employment or appointment to a class or classes of offices under the government of, or any local or other authority within, a State or Union territory.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Equality**

 
 
• The **right to equality guarantees that everyone is treated fairly before the law prohibits discrimination for a variety of reasons treats all applicants for public employment equally, and outlaws untouchability and titles (such as Sir, Rai Bahadur, etc.).**
 
• In accordance with Article 16, there are exclusions from the right to equal opportunity in matters of public employment to protect the interests of the society's weaker and more vulnerable **groups, such as women, children, members of the backward classes (SC/ST), and minorities.**

questions.question: Zero hour in political jagron referes to

options.text: day when no business in Parliament is done

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**question-answer session**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The time following question hour in Parliament is known as Zero Hour. In political jargon, Zero hour refers to question-answer session**.
 
• The Zero hour **starts immediately after the question hour and lasts until the agenda for the day is taken up**.
 
• In other words, the time gap between the question hour and the agenda is known as Zero hour.
 
• Zero hour usually **starts at 12 noon**, whereby MPs can raise their question about **issues of urgent public importance**.
 
• Zero hour is **not mentioned in the rules of procedure**. It is an **Indian innovation** in the field of Parliamentary procedures and has **been in existence since 1962.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adjournment Motion**

 
 
• **​It is introduced in the Parliament to draw the attention of the House to a definite matter of urgent public importance**.
 
• The discussion on an adjournment motion should** last for not less than two hours and 30 minutes (2.5 hours)**.
 
• It needs the **support of 50 members** to be admitted.
 
• **As it interrupts the normal business of the House, it is regarded as an extraordinary motion.**
 
• It involves an** element of censure against the government** means if passed the council ministers are bound to seek confidence in Lok Sabha otherwise they have to resign.
 
• As the Council of ministers is not liable to Rajya Sabha for its actions, hence **Rajya Sabha is not permitted to make use of this motion.**
 
 
 
• **Adjournment **
 
 
• ​An adjournment time means the suspension of the work in a sitting for a specified period of time.
 
• It can be hours, days or weeks. **Adjournment sine die **means terminating the sitting for an indefinite period of time.
 
• The **power of the adjournment and adjournment sine die both lies with the Presiding officer **of the House.
 
• The presiding officer declares adjournment sine die when the working or business of the House is completed.

• **Rice **is the major **Indian crops** requires high **temperature (above 25°C)** and high **humidity**.
 
• For **Kharif** **crops**, high temperatures** (over 25 °C)** and high **humidity **are necessary.
 
• It needs annual precipitation of at least **100 cm**.
 
• It flourishes with **irrigation **in places with little **rainfall**. India's **northern **and **northern-eastern plains**,** coastal regions**, and deltaic areas are all where **rice **is farmed.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Although the phrase may sometimes be used to refer to **wild **or **uncultivated **variants of **Oryza**, wild rice is typically used to refer to species of the **genera Zizania and Porteresia**.

questions.question: Which of the following is responsible for nitrogen fixation ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bacteria**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rhizobium bacterium** is responsible for nitrogen fixation.
 
• It is found in soil which lives in a symbiotic relationship with roots of leguminous plants like peas, groundnuts, lentil, peanuts, etc.
 
• It produces nodules at the root of plants and converts the atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia which can be used in the growth and development of plants.
 
• Plants provide the bacteria with organic compounds made by photosynthesis.
 
• Thus, it lives in symbiotic relation with leguminous plants in which both the species are in a win-win situation and doesn’t harm anyone\

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fungus**:

 
 
• Fungi are essential decomposers in ecosystems, breaking down dead organic matter and recycling nutrients.
 
• They form mutualistic relationships with plant roots called mycorrhizae, which enhance water and nutrient absorption.
 
• Fungi do not fix nitrogen but play a crucial role in nutrient cycling and soil health.
 
 
 
• **Virus**:
 
 
• Viruses are microscopic infectious agents that replicate only inside the living cells of organisms.
 
• They can infect all types of life forms, from animals and plants to microorganisms, including bacteria and archaea.
 
• Viruses lack the cellular machinery for nitrogen fixation and are primarily known for causing diseases.
 
 
 
• **Insects**:
 
 
• Insects are a diverse group of arthropods with roles in pollination, decomposition, and as part of the food web.
 
• They contribute to nutrient cycling and soil aeration. While insects don't fix nitrogen, their activities, such as waste decomposition, indirectly influence soil fertility and ecosystem health.

questions.question: In Slide Show, which option ensures that only a specific set of slides is played during an MS PowerPoint 2019 presentation without creating a new file?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Use Custom Slide Show**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Custom Slide Show** is a feature in **Microsoft PowerPoint** that allows users to create a personalized slideshow by selecting a subset of slides from the main presentation.
 
• This option helps in tailoring presentations to specific audiences without the need to create multiple files or presentations. *Hence, it ensures that only the selected slides are displayed during the slideshow.*
 
• To use the feature, navigate to the **Slide Show tab**, click on **Custom Slide Show**, and then create a new custom slideshow by selecting the desired slides.
 
• The feature ensures flexibility and customization, making it ideal for scenarios where the same presentation is used for different purposes or audiences.
 
• This method does not modify the original presentation, preserving the integrity of the main file while allowing specific slide selections to be showcased.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Use Custom Slide Show__.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Browsed at a Kiosk:**

 
 
• This option sets the presentation to run in **kiosk mode**, meaning it loops continuously and disables manual slide advancement.
 
• It is generally used for trade shows or information booths where the presentation runs unattended.
 
• This mode is not suitable for selecting specific slides to display. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Show Slides: From-To Range:**
 
 
• This option allows users to define a specific range of slides (e.g., slides 5 to 10) to display during the slideshow.
 
• While this provides limited customization, it does not allow for skipping random slides or creating multiple custom presentations. *Hence, this option is also not the best choice.*
 
 
 
• **Loop Continuously Until Esc:**
 
 
• This option is used to enable the slideshow to run in a continuous loop until the user presses the **Escape** key.
 
• It is useful for unattended presentations but does not provide any customization of slide selection. *Hence, this is not the correct option.*

questions.question: Which pH range of rain water is considered as indicator of acid rain?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

**pH:**

__
 
• pH should be thought of simply as a number which **indicates** the** acidic or basic** **nature **of a solution.
 
• The** pH** of a **neutral solution is 7.**
 
• Values** less than 7 **on the pH scale represent an **acidic solution.**

**Explanation:**__

**Acid rain:**

__
 
• When the pH of the **rainwater drops below 5.6,** it is called **acid rain.**
 
• Acid rain refers to the ways in which **acid** from the **atmosphere** is **deposited on the earth’s surface**.
 
• **Oxides of nitrogen** and sulphur which are **acidic in nature** can be **blown by the wind** along with **solid particles** in the **atmosphere** and finally settle down either on the ground as **dry deposition** or in** water, fog and snow** as wet deposition.
 
• Acid rain is a byproduct of a variety of **human activities** that emit the oxides of **sulphur and nitrogen** into the **atmosphere.**

**Thus, below the 5.6 pH range of rainwater is considered an indicator of acid rain.__**

questions.question: In a badminton singles game, if both the players are on 29 points then at what point will one of them win the game?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**30th point**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In a game of badminton,** under the current rules set by the** Badminton World Federation, a singles match is won by the player who first scores 21 points, unless the score reaches 20-all.**
 
• When the score is tied at **20-all, the side which gains a two-point lead first wins that game.**
 
• However, if the score becomes **29-all, the side scoring the 30th point wins that game.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **About Badminton:**
 
• **Playing Area:**
 
 
• **​**Unlike doubles, the entire width of the court is not used in a singles match.
 
• The boundaries are defined by the outer lines of the length and the inner lines of the width.
 
 
 
• **Scoring:**
 
 
• **​**A match consists of the best of three games of 21 points each.
 
• Every time there's a serve, a point is scored.
 
• The side winning a rally adds a point to its score.
 
 
 
• **Service Rules:**
 
 
• **​**At the start of the game, the server serves from the right service court if their score is even, and from the left if their score is odd.
 
• After winning a point, the server switches service courts and continues serving.
 
 
 
• **Tied Score:**
 
 
• **​**In case the score reaches 20-all, the side which gains a two-point lead first, wins that game.
 
• However, if the score becomes 29-all, the side scoring the 30th point wins that game.
 
 
 
• **Strategy:**
 
 
• Singles badminton requires excellent control over the shuttlecock because the objective is to move the opponent around the court, making them run back and forth in order to create space.
 
• Stamina and agility are key, as the player has to cover the entire court by themselves.

questions.question: What is the effect of using Ctrl + J in MS Word, and how is it distinct from Ctrl + Shift + J?

options.text: Ctrl + J left-aligns; Ctrl + Shift + J right-aligns
Ctrl + J justifies text; Ctrl + Shift + J applies distributed justification where last line is also stretched
Ctrl + J centers text; Ctrl + Shift + J varies justification

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ctrl + J justifies text; Ctrl + Shift + J applies distributed justification where the last line is also stretched**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ctrl + J:** This shortcut is used to **justify text** in MS Word, aligning text evenly between the left and right margins, creating a clean and professional appearance.
 
• **Ctrl + Shift + J:** This shortcut applies **distributed justification**, ensuring that the text is evenly spaced across the entire width of the page, including the last line, which is stretched.
 
• Distributed justification (Ctrl + Shift + J) is particularly useful in formatting documents where **full block alignment** is desired, such as legal or academic documents.
 
• The distinction lies in the treatment of the last line: **Ctrl + J** does not stretch the last line, whereas **Ctrl + Shift + J** does.
 
• Both shortcuts ensure proper alignment for readability but are applied based on formatting preferences for specific document types.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Justify Alignment:**

 
 
• Text is aligned evenly along both left and right margins, creating a clean block of text.
 
• Used in professional documents, essays, and reports for a polished appearance.
 
• Does not stretch the last line unless specified.
 
 
 
• **Distributed Justification:**
 
 
• Text is spaced evenly across the width of the page, including the last line.
 
• Ideal for legal documents, certificates, or specific formatting requirements.
 
• Can sometimes result in uneven spacing between words.
 
 
 
• **Formatting in MS Word:**
 
 
• MS Word offers multiple alignment options, including left, center, right, justify, and distributed, catering to various document styles.
 
• Users can also customize margins and spacing to enhance the document's aesthetic and readability.
 
• Keyboard shortcuts enable quicker formatting without navigating through menus.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Both justify and distributed justification are used in professional and academic contexts.
 
• Justify is common in essays, reports, and newspapers.
 
• Distributed justification is frequently used in legal documentation and certificates.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Keyboard Shortcuts:** Keyboard shortcuts like **Ctrl + J** and **Ctrl + Shift + J** save time and enhance productivity in text formatting.
 
• **Alignment Importance:** Proper alignment improves the readability and professional appeal of documents.
 
• **Spacing Considerations:** Distributed justification can sometimes result in uneven spacing, requiring careful review.
 
• **Customization:** MS Word provides advanced tools for customizing alignment, spacing, and margins to suit user preferences.

questions.question: When did the UNDP publish the first Human Development Report?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**In 1990**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first **Human Development Report** was published by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in 1990**.
 
• The report introduced the Human Development Index (HDI), which measures a country's average achievements in three basic aspects of human development: health, education, and income.
 
• The **HDI** has since become a widely used tool to assess and compare the level of human development across different countries.
 
• The report aims to shift the focus of development economics from national income accounting to people-centered policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The UNDP was established in 1965 and is headquartered in New York City.
 
• It works in approximately 170 countries and territories to eradicate poverty and reduce inequalities through sustainable development.
 
• The Human Development Report is an annual publication that provides an update on the state of human development worldwide.
 
• The HDI is a composite index that takes into account life expectancy, education level, and per capita income indicators.
 
• Over the years, the report has expanded its scope to cover various aspects of human development, including gender inequality, poverty, and environmental sustainability.
 
• The theme of the first Human Development Report was "Concept and Measurement of Human Development."
